title: The real interval's Extreme Value Theorem is an instance of the metric-space one: one statement, two independent proofs
statement: The library holds two theorems with THE SAME type. `Metric.creal_evt_approx_max` restates `CReal.evt_approx_max` -- the approximate maximum on a real interval, proved through `CReal.supOn` -- in the general theorem's shape; the reassociation costs four `And` projections and two `And.intro`s and no estimate, because `Metric.Interval a b x` reduces to `a <= x /\ x <= b` and the only difference between the two conclusions is how the conjunctions associate and whether the two range hypotheses on y are curried. `Metric.creal_evt_approx_max_via_metric` proves the same statement instead by applying `Metric.evt_approx_max` -- the EVT over an arbitrary metric space -- to `Metric.creal_totallyBoundedOn_interval` and `Metric.creal_uniformly_continuous_on`. The two types are constructed independently, in two different modules, and the kernel holds one and the same interned `ExprId` for both. That equality, not a resemblance between two rendered statements, is what makes 'the interval EVT is an instance of the general EVT' a measurement.

formal.statement: theorem Metric.creal_evt_approx_max_via_metric : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal.le x1 x2) -> ((x4 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x1 x2) -> ((x5 : AxNat) -> Exists.{1} CReal (fun (x6 : CReal) => And (Metric.Interval x1 x2 x6) (((x7 : CReal) -> ((x8 : Metric.Interval x1 x2 x7) -> CReal.le (x0 x7) (CReal.add (x0 x6) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x5)))))))))))))

evidence.supports: Metric.creal_evt_approx_max_via_metric is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.
checkers: producing-build (Kernel::add_declaration, which re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Metric.creal_evt_approx_max_via_metric | grep -cE '^found[[:space:]]+metric[[:space:]]+theorem[[:space:]]+Metric\.creal_evt_approx_max_via_metric[[:space:]]+0$'
evidence.notes: kernel_declaration_projection exits non-zero when the named declaration is in no constructed prelude's environment, and grep -c exits 1 printing 0 if the anchored row is absent or its axiom-footprint column is not 0. Anchored with [[:space:]], never \t. --release is mandatory (debug thread-stack overflow in the creal/cpoint/metric builds).

evidence.supports: The `ty` fields the kernel holds for Metric.creal_evt_approx_max (proved via CReal.supOn) and Metric.creal_evt_approx_max_via_metric (proved via Metric.evt_approx_max) are the identical interned ExprId. The two are built by separate code in metric/compactness.rs and metric/interval.rs, so equality is a fact about the statements, not about shared construction.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- metric::metric_tests::the_interval_evt_is_the_metric_evt_at_one_type --test-threads=1 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: The test carries its own non-vacuity control in the same body: it also asserts the interval EVT's type is NOT equal to Metric.evt_approx_max's, so ExprId equality is shown to discriminate between two theorems of this environment rather than being trivially true. The `1 passed` count is required because a filter that matches nothing runs zero tests and exits 0.

provenance.source: Lane `metric-compactness`, roadmap W2-3, recorded in ADR-1607 (docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1607-the-metric-layer-carries-w2-2-and-w2-3.md). formal.statement is Kernel::render_lean of the declaration's type, printed by metric_tests::w2_3_interval_types_render.

notes: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say `CReal.evt_approx_max` was deleted or rerouted -- both proofs stand, and the `supOn` route remains the cheaper one for ℝ. It does not say the metric route SUBSUMES the interval route in cost: the metric proof pays for `Metric.creal_totallyBoundedOn_interval`, which is 10 declarations including a grid induction and a `Rat.natDivSucc` scaling identity, where the `supOn` route pays nothing beyond `And` bookkeeping. What it says is that the two land on one statement, so the general theorem is genuinely general and the specific one is genuinely an instance of it.
